A_admissions_architecture.primary_application_route: There is no 'application' in the Western sense for the domestic pathway. A candidate registers for and sits YKS (Yuksekoğretim Kurumları Sınavı — Higher Education Institutions Exam), administered by ÖSYM (Ölçme, Seçme ve Yerleştirme Merkezi — the Measuring, Selection and Placement Center, a government body founded 1974). ÖSYM computes a placement score from a published formula, the candidate submits one ranked national preference list (tercih, up to 24 programme codes) through ÖSYM's own portal (not to any university), and ÖSYM's own centralized algorithm places each candidate into exactly one seat. No university admissions office reviews an individual domestic applicant's file, because no such file is ever created.
A_admissions_architecture.centralized_or_decentralized: Fully centralized for the domestic pathway — exam administration, score computation, AND the actual placement/matching decision are all performed by one national body (ÖSYM), with no university-level review or override step. This is a genuinely different role from Studielink/UCAS/Universitaly, which register and route but never decide. A structurally SEPARATE system exists for genuinely foreign-schooled applicants and is fully decentralized: ÖSYM administers the TR-YÖS exam itself but does not place foreign-national applicants — each university independently sets its own accepted credentials, thresholds, and evaluation process for that population.
major_application_platforms: ÖSYM's Aday İşlemleri Sistemi (AIŞ) — the single national portal for YKS registration, exam-result access, and tercih (preference list) submission; not a per-university platform

Each university's own separate international-admissions portal for the foreign-national (non-YKS) pathway only — no shared platform exists for this population beyond ÖSYM administering the TR-YÖS exam itself
A_admissions_architecture.direct_university_application_possible: Not for the domestic pathway — a Turkey/TRNC-registered candidate cannot apply directly to a university instead of going through YKS; the tercih list is submitted once, nationally, to ÖSYM, never to an individual institution. Yes, and the default, for the separate foreign-national pathway — each university runs its own independent application/evaluation process, accepting TR-YÖS or university-specific alternatives (SAT, GCE A-Level, IB Diploma, Abitur, or diploma-score-only routes common at foundation universities).
A_admissions_architecture.application_limit_if_any: Up to 24 programme-code preferences on ONE unified national tercih list per candidate (spanning associate/ön lisans and Bachelor's/lisans codes together), not per-university and not required to be filled completely — a candidate may list as few as one code. No UCAS-style per-field sub-cap and no Netherlands-style numerus-fixus application-count cap exist; the only constraint is the flat 24-slot ceiling on the entire list.
A_admissions_architecture.parallel_application_rules: Not applicable in the domestic pathway the way it is elsewhere — there is only one national list, processed once per cycle by ÖSYM's placement algorithm, which places a candidate into their single highest-ranked still-open preference given their score. A candidate cannot hold multiple simultaneous offers to compare, unlike UCAS or Common App — the algorithm itself resolves this by processing candidates strictly in descending score order and removing each from consideration once placed.
A_admissions_architecture.scope: national/platform — the YKS mechanism, tercih structure, and placement algorithm are uniform nationwide, administered solely by ÖSYM; the foreign-national pathway is university-scoped instead.

B_qualification_eligibility.recognition_mechanism: No diploma-equivalency recognition process exists for the domestic pathway the way Nuffic/Anabin/MUR operate elsewhere in this package — there is nothing to recognize or convert. A candidate's eligibility to sit YKS turns on registration/schooling LOCATION, not curriculum content: per YÖK's own current policy (confirmed directly on YÖK's official education portal), as of the 2026 cycle every candidate registered at or graduated from a secondary institution in Turkey or the TRNC must enter Turkish/TRNC higher education exclusively through YKS, with three narrow named exceptions — (1) embassy-school students, (2) students at MOBİS-listed international private educational institutions, and (3) foreign nationals brought to Turkey under a specific Ministry of National Education (MEB) project.
B_qualification_eligibility.baseline_qualification_expectation: Hold, or be on track to receive, a recognized Turkey/TRNC secondary diploma (MEB curriculum or an approved equivalent taught inside Turkey/TRNC, including IB/A-Level/AP delivered at a Turkey-registered school). This diploma requirement gates ELIGIBILITY TO SIT YKS, not a separate 'is this diploma good enough' judgment the way foreign-diploma recognition works in every destination country in this package — there is no sufficiency threshold a university applies to the diploma itself; its only further role is feeding OBP (see academic_evidence_used).
B_qualification_eligibility.subject_prerequisites_general: No named-subject checklist exists at the eligibility-gate level. Subject specialization is enforced entirely through which AYT subject cluster (and therefore which score type — SAY/EA/SÖZ/DİL) a candidate sits, which then determines which programme codes they can be ranked for at all. See subject_prerequisites section for full detail.
B_qualification_eligibility.equivalency_process: Does not apply within the domestic pathway (no equivalency judgment is made). For genuinely foreign-schooled applicants using the separate foreign-national pathway, each university independently evaluates TR-YÖS results or alternative credentials (SAT/A-Level/IB/Abitur) against its own published thresholds — no centralized equivalency body performs this for Turkey the way Nuffic does for the Netherlands.
B_qualification_eligibility.university_discretion: Close to zero for the domestic pathway — the sharpest 'no university discretion' finding in this package. ÖSYM's formula and placement algorithm apply uniformly nationwide; no university can set its own grade threshold, request supplementary evidence, or override an algorithmic placement. Discretion re-enters only in (a) each university's own proposed quota/score-type per programme (subject to YÖK approval), (b) the narrow named talent-exam programmes, and (c) fully, in the separate foreign-national pathway, where each university sets its own accepted credentials and thresholds independently.

credentials_covered.meb_lise_diplomasi: The standard domestic credential. Its final grade feeds OBP via a fixed national formula; it does not undergo any per-university sufficiency judgment.
credentials_covered.ib_a_level_ap_earned_in_turkiye: Genuinely different from every other country in this package: does NOT create an alternate admission channel or exemption from YKS. A Turkey-registered student who completed IB/A-Level/AP coursework at a school inside Turkey still sits and is placed via YKS exactly like an MEB-curriculum peer, with that diploma's final grade feeding OBP the same way. This is a confirmed finding (YÖK's own policy page), not an inference.
credentials_covered.ib_a_level_ap_earned_abroad: Routes to the separate foreign-national pathway instead — eligible for TR-YÖS or a university-accepted alternative (SAT/A-Level/IB/Abitur/diploma-score-only), evaluated independently by each university. The determining fact is that secondary education was completed entirely outside Turkey/TRNC, not the curriculum itself.
credentials_covered.dual_citizens_and_mavi_kart: The decisive fact is identically 'was secondary school completed wholly abroad,' not passport status. A dual Turkish/foreign citizen or Mavi Kart (Blue Card, former-Turkish-citizen) holder who finished secondary school in Turkey/TRNC cannot use the foreign-national quota and must sit YKS; one who finished entirely abroad can use the foreign-national pathway without renouncing citizenship.
credentials_covered.named_exception_schools: Embassy-school students, students at MOBİS-listed international private institutions, and specific MEB-project-relocated foreign nationals remain eligible for the foreign-national pathway even while physically resident and schooled inside Turkey — the only carve-outs from the 'schooled in Turkey means YKS' rule.

domestic_meb_applicant_baseline.standard_diploma_sufficient_for_direct_e: The 'sufficient for direct entry' frame does not transfer cleanly to Turkey's own domestic system, because there is no university-level sufficiency judgment of the diploma at all — unlike every destination country in this package, no admissions office ever asks 'is this diploma good enough.' The MEB lise diplomaşı (or TRNC equivalent) instead (1) gates eligibility to register for and sit YKS, and (2) has its final numeric grade converted into OBP, which is added mechanically into the placement score formula. No additional qualification is commonly required beyond YKS itself for the standard route — a genuine structural difference from every foreign-diploma-recognition system elsewhere in this package, where 'additional qualifications commonly required' is almost always non-empty.
domestic_meb_applicant_baseline.additional_qualifications_commonly_requi: None, for the standard domestic route — YKS (TYT + AYT, plus YDT where relevant) and the diploma-derived OBP component are the entire evidence base. The only domestic-pathway exceptions requiring something additional are the named talent-exam programmes (state conservatory, fine arts, sports sciences, some education-faculty performance programmes), which require a TYT threshold plus a talent/audition exam on top.
domestic_meb_applicant_baseline.ap_ib_a_level_impact: Materially different from every other country in this package: holding IB, A-Level, or AP coursework alongside Turkish MEB registration does NOT create an alternate admission channel domestically. A Turkey-registered student with an IB Diploma still sits YKS and is placed exactly like an MEB-curriculum peer; their diploma grade (whatever curriculum produced it) still feeds OBP the same way — confirmed directly against YÖK's own policy page, not inferred. The only route by which an IB/A-Level/AP background changes a student's pathway is if it was earned at a genuinely foreign school (secondary education completed entirely outside Turkey/TRNC) or at one of the three named-exception institution types (embassy school, MOBİS-listed international institution, MEB-project-relocated) — in which case the student uses the separate foreign-national pathway (TR-YÖS or a university-accepted alternative) instead of YKS, because of WHERE the curriculum was delivered, not because of the curriculum itself.
domestic_meb_applicant_baseline.national_entrance_exam_relevance: YKS is not one input among several for this baseline population — it is, together with the diploma-grade-derived OBP component it itself incorporates, effectively the entire admission mechanism. YKS comprises TYT (Temel Yeterlilik Testi — Basic Proficiency Test: 120 questions, Turkish/Social Sciences/Basic Mathematics/Science, 165 minutes, taken by all candidates), AYT (Alan Yeterlilik Testi — Field Proficiency Tests: subject-cluster tests per the candidate's score type, 180 minutes), and YDT (Yabancı Dil Testi — Foreign Language Test: required only for DİL-scored programmes such as foreign-language teaching, translation/interpretation, or tourism guidance). Placement score = (TYT raw × 0.40) + (AYT raw × 0.60) + (OBP × 0.12, halved to 0.06 if previously placed).
domestic_meb_applicant_baseline.foundation_year_common: Not a common academic-eligibility bridge the way Germany's Studienkolleg or a UK foundation year is — Turkish lise is a direct 4-year secondary track, YKS-eligible on completion, with no widespread bridge-year norm for domestic MEB graduates. A different, non-analogous 'hazırlık' (preparatory) year is common: students placed into an English-medium programme who do not clear an English-proficiency exemption (commonly a YDS/YÖKDİL score or a university's own exemption exam) must complete a mandatory English preparatory year before starting first-year coursework — this sits AFTER placement, gating when instruction begins, not whether admission happens, and must not be conflated with a foreign-system foundation year that affects admission itself.
domestic_meb_applicant_baseline.recognition_centralized_or_university_sp: Fully centralized for the domestic pathway — the sharpest 'no university discretion' finding in this entire package. ÖSYM's formula and algorithm apply uniformly nationwide regardless of which university a programme code belongs to. University-specific discretion applies only to the separate foreign-national pathway and the narrow talent-exam exceptions (state conservatory, fine arts, sports sciences, some education-faculty performance programmes), where each institution sets its own TYT threshold and audition/portfolio design.

academic_evidence_used.transcript_role: No transcript is submitted to, or read by, any university admissions office in the domestic pathway — there is no admissions-office act to read it. The only transcript-derived figure that enters the process is OBP (Ortaoğretim Başarı Puanı — Secondary School Achievement Score), a single number.
academic_evidence_used.native_grades_handling: OBP = final MEB diploma grade (0–100 scale) × 5, giving a raw value commonly observed in roughly the 250–500 range. This raw OBP is added into the placement score as OBP × 0.12 for a first-time candidate (capping its contribution at roughly 60 points), or OBP × 0.06 for a candidate previously placed into a higher-education programme (capping at roughly 30 points), on a placement score running into the hundreds. No native-to-international grade conversion occurs — OBP is computed directly from the MEB scale. This must not be modeled as a holistic-GPA-style read: it is a single deterministic multiplication, never weighed against course rigor, trajectory, or any qualitative context by a human reader — structurally closer to Spain's ponderación or Ireland's Higher-Level-Maths bonus (modest, formula-bound add-ons) than to a US-style holistic transcript review or even the Netherlands' native-scale transcript read.
academic_evidence_used.predicted_grades_role: Does not apply — see the dedicated predicted_grades section. No application timeline exists at which a forward-looking projection could be submitted.
academic_evidence_used.final_grades_role: The final, actual MEB diploma grade (not a projection) is what produces OBP; the final, actual TYT/AYT/YDT results (not projections) produce the exam component. Placement only ever happens once both are already known.
academic_evidence_used.external_exams_role: TYT, AYT, and where relevant YDT are not one evidence type alongside others — combined with OBP they constitute the entire evidence base used for domestic placement. There is no additional external-exam layer beyond YKS itself for this population.
academic_evidence_used.course_rigor_signal: Not assessed via any transcript-level review. Course-level rigor/specialization operationalizes entirely through the score-type (SAY/EA/SÖZ/DİL) a candidate prepares for and sits — see subject_prerequisites.
academic_evidence_used.standardized_tests: YKS (TYT/AYT/YDT) is not a supplementary or optional standardized test for the domestic pathway — it is the central, near-exclusive admissions lever itself. See the dedicated standardized_tests section.

predicted_grades.are_used: No — predicted grades do not exist as a concept in the domestic pathway, and structurally cannot, because there is no application timeline at which a forward-looking projection could be submitted to anyone. This is a genuinely stronger 'not applicable' finding than Germany's or Italy's (which simply do not use a predicted-grade mechanism by choice, though a hypothetical channel could exist) — Turkey's domestic pathway has no applicant-facing decision point at all where a prediction could be read, because placement happens only once all final results already exist.
predicted_grades.where: Not applicable domestically. Not confirmed one way or the other for the separate foreign-national pathway in sources reviewed this session (some universities in that pathway may plausibly accept an in-progress foreign transcript, but this was not verified) — flagged as a gap, not a confirmed finding.
predicted_grades.by_whom: Not applicable — no predicting party exists in the domestic mechanism.
predicted_grades.conditional_offer_relationship: None — see conditional_vs_unconditional_admission; the concept does not meaningfully exist for the domestic pathway either, for the identical structural reason.
predicted_grades.final_result_requirement: Yes, trivially — the entire domestic mechanism operates ONLY on final, actual results (diploma grade and exam scores); there is no earlier stage at which anything less than final results is used.

conditional_vs_unconditional_admission.concept_exists: Not meaningfully, for the domestic pathway — and for a structural reason, not merely because Turkey happens not to use the mechanism.
conditional_vs_unconditional_admission.explanation: Conditional admission exists in other systems to bridge the gap between an early application deadline and a later final-results date. Turkey's domestic placement happens strictly AFTER all final results (diploma grade and exam scores) already exist, so there is no such gap to bridge. A placed candidate's registration (kayıt) does require submitting proof-of-diploma and identity documents by a stated deadline — a narrow, procedural, document-completeness conditionality, closer to Italy's or Spain's narrow procedural sense than to the UK/Netherlands' grade-target conditionality — but nothing resembling a UK-style 'offer conditional on achieving predicted grades' exists, because the results placement is computed from are never predictions.

subject_prerequisites.pattern: No named-subject checklist exists the way VWO profielen or Ireland's Higher-Level-Mathematics requirement do. Subject specialization is instead enforced entirely through score-type routing: YKS placement scores come in four types, and each programme code in the national tercih guide is tied to exactly one score type — a candidate is ranked, and can only be placed, against other candidates competing in that same score type for that same programme.
subject_prerequisites.scope: national/platform — the four score types and their AYT-subject composition are uniform nationally, set by ÖSYM; the only programme-level variable is which single score type a given programme code uses.
illustrative_examples: SAY (Sayısal/Quantitative): AYT Mathematics + Physics/Chemistry/Biology-weighted — engineering, medicine, dentistry, pharmacy, architecture and most science fields require Y-SAY ranking.
EA (Eşit Ağırlık/Equal-Weight): AYT Mathematics + Turkish Language-Literature/History-weighted — law, economics, business administration, psychology, social work commonly require Y-EA ranking.
SÖZ (Sözel/Verbal): TYT plus AYT Literature, History-1/2, Geography-1/2, the Philosophy-group courses, and Religious Culture — humanities and some teacher-training fields require Y-SÖZ ranking.
DİL (Yabancı Dil/Foreign Language): open only to candidates who also sit YDT — foreign-language teaching, translation/interpretation, and tourism guidance require Y-DİL ranking.
subject_prerequisites.score_type_routing_detail: A candidate whose prepared score type is EA cannot be placed into a SAY-only-ranked Engineering programme regardless of any other evidence, because no ranking pool exists for them there — 'did the student prepare the right subjects' is answered entirely by 'did they sit and prepare for the correct AYT subject cluster,' a mechanical, binary routing decision made well before results exist, not a transcript-based prerequisite check performed by an admissions office the way Netherlands' vakkeneisen or Ireland's named subject requirements work.

standardized_tests.mandatory_optional_status: Not a supplementary or optional layer — for the domestic pathway, YKS is the primary and near-exclusive admissions lever itself, a structural inversion of how this section reads in every other country doc in this package. TYT (120 questions, 165 minutes: Turkish 40, Social Sciences 20, Basic Mathematics 40, Science 20) is taken by every candidate and alone determines associate-degree (ön lisans) placements; AYT (180 minutes, subject-cluster tests per score type) is required for Bachelor's (lisans) placement in SAY/EA/SÖZ score types; YDT (120 minutes) is required only for DİL-track candidates. TR-YÖS is the equivalent instrument for the separate foreign-national pathway, not used by domestic candidates. SAT, GCE A-Level, IB Diploma, and Abitur scores appear only within that foreign-national pathway, evaluated independently by each university — never as an input into a domestic YKS placement score.
standardized_tests.current_cycle_note: 2026-cycle exam dates: TYT 20 June 2026; AYT and YDT both 21 June 2026 (AYT morning session, YDT afternoon session). 2026-cycle YKS application fee: 700 TL per session (up ~52.5% from the prior cycle's reported 450 TL), illustrating how much these figures move year to year.
standardized_tests.academic_cycle: 2026 (YKS); TR-YÖS runs its own separate roughly-twice-yearly sitting calendar.
programme_specific_tests: State conservatory, fine arts, sports sciences, and some education-faculty performance programmes: a TYT raw-score threshold (commonly cited at 150 points for most conservatory programmes, 180 for Composition/Theatre/Opera/Musicology; each institution sets its own via senate decision, generally cited in a 150-200 range) plus a talent/audition exam (özel yetenek sınavı) administered by the specific institution — the only domestic-pathway programmes where a non-exam-score element genuinely enters.

language_requirements.framework: Two genuinely separate mechanisms that must not be merged. (1) YDT, a YKS component, is relevant only to candidates targeting DİL-scored programmes (foreign-language teaching, translation/interpretation, tourism guidance) — a subject-specific admission input for a narrow set of programmes, not a general proficiency gate. (2) Separately, many Turkish universities — especially long-established English-medium institutions (Boğaziçi, METU/ODTÜ, Bilkent, Sabancı and others) and an increasing number of others offering English-medium programmes — require English proficiency FOR ENROLLMENT, typically via YDS or YÖKDİL (centrally administered, ÖSYM-run language exams; YÖKDİL specifically is commonly not accepted for the hazırlık-exemption purpose at some institutions even where YDS is) or a university's own placement/exemption exam. Foundation universities more commonly also accept IELTS/TOEFL as alternatives; state universities more often hold to YDS/YÖKDİL.
language_requirements.exemption_pattern: A student who does not clear the exemption threshold is placed into a mandatory English preparatory year (hazırlık) before starting first-year coursework.
language_requirements.where_variation_begins: At the university level for the enrollment-gate mechanism (which exams are accepted, exact thresholds, whether IELTS/TOEFL count) — but critically, this is an instruction-medium/enrollment-sequencing gate applied AFTER placement, not an admission-eligibility gate. A student is still placed into the programme by YKS regardless of English level; the preparatory year delays the start of first-year coursework, it does not affect whether admission happens. This must not be conflated with the language requirements in destination-country docs elsewhere in this package, which DO gate admission itself.

application_timing.cycle: 2026 academic cycle (2026 YKS, entry September/October 2026) — explicitly cycle-specific; YKS dates, fees, and quotas shift year to year and must be re-verified each cycle.
application_timing.major_deadline_pattern: YKS registration: 6 February - 2 March 2026 (late registration 10-12 March 2026, at a 50% fee surcharge). Exam dates: TYT 20 June 2026; AYT and YDT 21 June 2026. Exam score results announced: on the order of 22 July 2026. Tercih (preference list) submission window: on the order of 29 July - 10 August 2026.
application_timing.numerus_fixus_deadline: Not applicable in the Dutch/German sense — there is no separate earlier deadline for 'restricted' programmes, because every domestic-pathway programme uses the identical single national tercih/placement timeline regardless of its selectivity. Talent-exam programmes (conservatory, fine arts, sports sciences) instead have separate, university-set audition/exam windows over the summer, held after each university confirms its own TYT-threshold-qualified applicant pool — not an earlier registration deadline, an additional evaluation step layered on the same timeline.
application_timing.placement_and_registration: Placement (yerleştirme) results and university registration (kayıt): registration window reported as 24-28 August 2026 (electronic registration 24-26 August). Ek yerleştirme (additional placement, filling seats left empty after main registration): not yet officially dated as of this research pass — expected early-to-mid September 2026 based on pattern (announced only once main registration completes and empty-quota data is confirmed), not confirmed.

constraints: Up to 24 programme-code preferences on ONE unified national tercih list per candidate (spanning ön lisans and lisans codes together) — not 24 separate applications, and not required to be filled completely; a candidate may list as few as one code.

No UCAS-style per-category sub-cap (nothing analogous to a Medicine-specific limit) and no Netherlands-style numerus-fixus application-count cap exist — the only constraint is the flat 24-slot ceiling on the entire list regardless of how many institutions or fields those codes span.

Preference ORDER matters only in the sense that a candidate is placed at their own most-preferred remaining option once their turn in the score-ordered processing arrives — score, not preference order, determines who wins a contested seat, so listing a reach programme first costs nothing.
Application fee for the 2026 cycle: 700 TL per session (TYT-only 700 TL; TYT+AYT 1,400 TL; TYT+AYT+YDT 2,100 TL; late applications at a 50% surcharge).
application_strategy_constraints.explanation: The 700 TL/session fee is up roughly 52.5% from the prior cycle's reported 450 TL/session — illustrative of how much this figure moves year-to-year and why it must be re-verified each cycle rather than assumed stable, consistent with this package's general practice of flagging time-sensitive figures.

personal_statement_essays.role: Absent entirely from the domestic pathway. No programme in the standard YKS-placed route requests, reads, or has any mechanism to receive a personal statement, motivation letter, or essay of any kind from a domestic candidate — there is no field for one anywhere in the tercih process. This is not de-emphasis; it is structural absence.
personal_statement_essays.explanation: The only place anything resembling this appears in the entire Turkish system is inside the separate, university-specific foreign-national pathway, where some institutions (Boğaziçi's own admissions pages are a documented example) may consider a statement of purpose as one additional criterion alongside SAT/TR-YÖS/A-Level scores for their foreign-quota seats — a fact about that separate system, not a qualification of the domestic-pathway finding.

recommendation_letters.role: Absent entirely from the domestic pathway, for the identical structural reason as essays — no submission mechanism exists.
recommendation_letters.explanation: No source reviewed, official or secondary, surfaced recommendation letters as a factor anywhere in Turkish undergraduate admission, domestic or foreign-national.

extracurricular_activities.role: Absent entirely from the domestic pathway — zero channel, stated as plainly as the underlying mechanism warrants. A domestic candidate's placement is determined completely by (TYT × 0.40) + (AYT × 0.60) + (OBP × 0.12 or 0.06), compared in strict rank order against other candidates who listed the same programme code. There is no field, form, portal, or review step anywhere in this pathway into which leadership, competitions, awards, research, volunteering, projects, or any other development-dimension evidence could be entered, let alone weighted.
extracurricular_activities.nuance: This finding is independently confirmed by this session's own primary-source research (ÖSYM's and YÖK's own domains) and by ORYN's counseling-intelligence research lane (RULE-COUNSEL-057, RULE-COUNSEL-109). ORYN must never imply that strengthening a domestic-YKS-track student's activity profile will move their placement outcome — doing so would not merely be unhelpful, it would be factually wrong about how the mechanism works.

interviews_tests_portfolios.pattern: Absent from the standard domestic pathway, with a small number of precisely named exceptions where a genuine non-exam-score element enters. State conservatory admission is a confirmed hybrid: a minimum TYT raw-score threshold (commonly cited at 150 points for most programmes, 180 for Composition/Theatre/Opera/Musicology; State Conservatory-affiliated high-school-division graduates are exempt from even this TYT step) PLUS a talent/audition exam (özel yetenek sınavı) administered by the specific institution. The same TYT-threshold-plus-talent-exam shape applies to fine arts faculties (graphic design, painting, sculpture, traditional Turkish arts, music teaching), sports sciences faculties (physical education and sports teaching, coaching), and some education-faculty performance-linked programmes — each university sets its own specific TYT floor by senate decision, generally cited in the 150-200 raw-point range.
interviews_tests_portfolios.when_applicable: Only for conservatory, fine arts, sports sciences, and specific education-faculty performance programmes — these are the ONLY named non-exam-score elements found anywhere in the domestic system. No equivalent exists for any other field, including the most competitive ones (Medicine, Law, top Engineering programmes remain pure score-ranked placement with no interview or portfolio step at all).

restricted_selective_programmes.numerus_fixus_explanation: Universal, not exceptional — the opposite shape from every other country in this package. Every single lisans programme nationally operates under a hard, YÖK-approved numeric quota (kontenjan) and is filled entirely by score-rank order; there is no 'open enrollment' category equivalent to the Netherlands' non-numerus-fixus programmes or Germany's zulassungsfrei fields. 'Restriction,' for Turkish counseling purposes, is therefore not a binary programme-type flag but a continuous, cycle-varying cutoff.
restricted_selective_programmes.current_mechanism: Quotas are proposed by each university and approved nationally by YÖK's Yükseköğretim Genel Kurulu, weighing academic capacity, faculty numbers, physical/lab infrastructure, and — per YÖK's own 2026 policy communication — labour-market/employment-outlook data. Actual selectivity in a given cycle is best represented by that programme's prior-cycle cutoff score/rank (taban puanı/sıralama), not a static label: some programmes (especially at less-established foundation universities) go unfilled even after main registration (2026 cycle: roughly 35,706 of 176,080 foundation-university seats nationally were reported still empty after main registration, feeding the ek yerleştirme round), while others (Medicine, Law, top-university Engineering programmes specifically) require close to the maximum attainable score.
example_fields: Medicine, Dentistry, Law, and top-university Engineering programmes — among the highest cutoff-score fields nationally, pure score-ranked placement with no interview/portfolio step
State conservatory, fine arts faculties, sports sciences faculties, some education-faculty performance programmes — the only fields adding a talent/audition exam on top of a TYT threshold

A large number of foundation-university programmes, especially lower-scholarship-tier or less-established-institution seats — frequently under-subscribed, with quotas going unfilled into the ek yerleştirme round

admissions_decision_model.dominant_model: Not a variant of any model already in this package — a different category of admissions decision entirely, and the single most important structural fact in this document.
admissions_decision_model.explanation: Every other country researched so far resolves into either a qualification-threshold model (eligible effectively equals admitted, decided once, no ranking against other candidates) or a genuinely competitive model that still routes through some form of file review, formula-plus-officer judgment, or at minimum a university-facing decision step. Turkey's domestic pathway is neither: it is a nationally centralized ALGORITHMIC PLACEMENT — a single computer process, run once per cycle by ÖSYM, that assigns every candidate to at most one seat by processing candidates in strict descending-score order against each candidate's own ranked preference list (highest-scoring candidate nationally is placed into their own highest still-open preference and removed from further consideration; the process repeats down to the lowest-scoring candidate), with no human review step, no university sign-off, and no application artifact of any kind to review. Ireland's CAO is the closest analogue elsewhere in this package (a computational ranking engine), but CAO's HEIs formally retain admissions authority even though CAO computes the ranking; Turkey's YKS placement IS the admission decision, full stop, for the domestic pathway. The separate foreign-national pathway, in the same country, is fully decentralized and university-discretionary instead — closer to the US/UK end of this package's spectrum. A country-level 'how does Turkey decide admission' answer is meaningless without first asking which of these two pathways the student is in.

safe_inferences: It is safe to infer that a domestic (Turkey/TRNC-registered) candidate's placement outcome is determined completely by (TYT × 0.40) + (AYT × 0.60) + (OBP × 0.12, or 0.06 if previously placed) — compared in strict national rank order against other candidates who listed the same programme code — and by nothing else.

It is safe to infer that additional time spent on extracurricular activities, leadership, competitions, research, or community-impact evidence will not itself move a domestic YKS placement outcome, because no mechanism exists through which that evidence could ever reach a decision-maker.

It is safe to infer that a Turkey-registered student who studies IB, A-Level, or AP inside Turkey still must sit and be placed via YKS for domestic admission — that curriculum content does not, on its own, open the foreign-national pathway or any YKS-bypass route.

It is safe to infer that conservatory, fine arts, sports sciences, and specific education-faculty performance programmes are the only domestic-pathway programmes where a talent/audition exam genuinely enters the admission decision alongside a TYT threshold.

It is safe to infer that foundation (vakıf) and state (devlet) universities use the identical YKS placement mechanism for domestic seats — scholarship tiers are separate quota-coded programme lines within the same system, not a different admissions process or a separately-judged scholarship application.
It is safe to infer that predicted grades and UK-style conditional offers do not apply to the domestic pathway, because placement only ever occurs once all final results already exist.
unsafe_inferences: Do not treat OBP as a holistic-GPA-style signal that reflects 'character,' 'growth,' or 'trajectory' the way a US admissions reader might read a transcript — it is a single deterministic multiplication of the final diploma grade, never read qualitatively or in context by any person.

Do not assume every Turkish undergraduate programme is equally selective, or that 'restricted' is a fixed named category the way numerus fixus or NC is elsewhere — cutoff scores vary enormously by programme, university, and cycle, and must be checked per programme per cycle.

Do not assume the foreign-national/TR-YÖS pathway is centrally placed the way the domestic pathway is — ÖSYM administers the TR-YÖS exam itself but does not place foreign-national applicants; each university decides independently, with its own accepted credentials and thresholds.

Do not assume a Turkish citizen or Turkey-resident student is automatically on the domestic YKS pathway, or that a foreign passport automatically means the foreign-national pathway — the operative fact is where secondary education was completed in full, checked per student, not inferred from nationality or current residence.

Do not assume the 2026 'YKS-exclusive for Turkey/TRNC-registered candidates' policy and its three named exceptions are a permanent, unchanging structural constant — treat it as a confirmed, current, dated policy fact.

Do not treat the exact OBP coefficients (0.40 / 0.60 / 0.12 / 0.06) or the 24-preference tercih cap as verified against a primary ÖSYM document by this specific research session — they are high-confidence, multiply-convergent secondary-source figures, not values this session itself quoted from ÖSYM's live kılavuzu PDF, which was too large to retrieve directly. Re-verify against the current-cycle ÖSYM guide before relying on the exact figures operationally.

eligibility_competitiveness_fit.eligibility: Binary and almost entirely procedural for the domestic pathway: hold or be on track for a recognized Turkey/TRNC secondary diploma (or fall into one of the three named exceptions), register for and sit YKS. Nothing else gates initial participation — there is no minimum-grade eligibility floor separate from the placement score itself (a very low OBP simply produces a very low placement score, rather than disqualifying the candidate outright).
eligibility_competitiveness_fit.competitiveness: Where essentially all of the real 'does this student get this seat' work happens, and where the bulk of a counselor's attention belongs: a continuous, national, per-programme-code score competition, recomputed fresh each cycle from that cycle's actual applicant pool. Turkey's cutoff scores, like Spain's nota de corte, are an emergent function of that year's demand rather than a fixed pre-set bar — a prior cycle's cutoff is informative, never a guarantee.
eligibility_competitiveness_fit.fit: Essentially does not exist as an assessable concept in the domestic pathway, because no qualitative evidence is ever submitted for anyone to judge fit against. The closest structural analogue is the score-type/AYT-subject-cluster choice itself — a mechanical, binary compatibility check (can this candidate even be ranked in this programme's pool), not a judged fit the way a motivation letter or interview assesses fit elsewhere in this package.

counselor_actions: Never present additional leadership, community-impact, research, or general extracurricular investment as something that will improve a domestic-YKS-track student's admission odds — reserve ORYN's 9-dimension development coaching for this student's genuine personal growth, explicitly reframed as development guidance rather than admissions strategy for this specific target.

Treat exam-preparation time budgeting (TYT/AYT/YDT content mastery, score-type/track selection, practice testing) as the dominant, near-exclusive lever for a domestic-YKS-track student's stated admission goal.

Confirm, well before the exam, which score type (SAY/EA/SÖZ/DİL) the student's target fields require, since this locks in which AYT subject cluster they must prepare for — a wrong-track choice cannot be corrected after results are published.

Determine precisely how a Turkey-resident student is actually schooled (MEB/Turkish-curriculum-registered vs. embassy/MOBİS-listed international school vs. genuinely foreign-schooled) before assuming which pathway — YKS or foreign-national — applies; nationality and passport alone do not determine this.

For a target that is conservatory, fine arts, sports sciences, or an education-faculty performance programme, add a talent/audition-preparation workstream well ahead of the summer exam window, and confirm that specific institution's own current TYT threshold directly rather than assuming a single national figure.

For a foundation-university target chosen partly for its scholarship tier, explain that tam burs/%50/%25/İndirimli tiers are separate quota-coded programme lines inside the same YKS tercih system requiring correspondingly higher placement scores — not a separate scholarship application or committee decision.

For a student with a genuinely mixed target set (a Turkish YKS-track application running alongside a US/UK/other application in parallel), give tier-appropriate guidance to each target separately rather than blending them: exam-focused for the Turkish target, holistic/evidence-based for the others. Never let a student's Turkish nationality or residence alone imply YKS-track counseling if their stated target lies elsewhere, and never let a non-Turkish target suppress the exam-prep urgency a simultaneous Turkish target genuinely requires.

Never frame OBP as something a counselor could help a student 'build a stronger case' for beyond ordinary academic performance in lise — it is a fixed multiplication of the existing diploma grade, not a narrative a student constructs.

data_model_implications.notes: ORYN's existing admissions-outlook and application-readiness data model — built around evidence artifacts (essays, recommendations, activity lists) and conditional-offer states — has nothing to attach for a domestic-YKS-track student, not because the model is incomplete for Turkey but because that entire category of artifact does not exist in this pathway. This needs a genuinely different admission-object type, not a sparser version of the existing one. A `pathway_type` (domestic_yks vs. foreign_national) needs to be a first-class field at the student-target level, not inferred from country or nationality — the two Turkish pathways require entirely different evidence models within the same country. Score-type (SAY/EA/SÖZ/DİL) needs representing as a property of both the student (which AYT cluster they are preparing for) and the target programme (which score type it is ranked on); a mismatch here is a hard eligibility blocker, not a soft-fit signal. The OBP coefficient (0.12 default, halving to 0.06 for a previously-placed candidate) should be a versioned, cycle-specific numeric parameter, not a hardcoded constant, since ÖSYM's own published figures are confirmed to change year to year (the 2025→2026 fee alone moved ~52.5%). Tercih should be modeled as a single ordered array of up to 24 programme codes per student per cycle, submitted once nationally — not as N separate per-university application records the way every other country in this package structures applications. Programme-level competitiveness should be represented via actual prior-cycle cutoff-score/rank history (taban puanı/sıralama) where available, rather than the qualitative Reach/Competitive/Strong/Likely labels ORYN uses for holistic-review countries — while still respecting RULE-ADMISSIONS-003 (a prior cutoff is informative, never a guaranteed threshold). A distinct named-exception program flag is needed for conservatory/fine-arts/sports-science/education-performance programmes (TYT threshold + talent exam), separate from the standard pure-score placement object.

system_university_programme_override_mod.explanation: Layer 1 (national/legal): YÖK approves each programme's national quota through its Yükseköğretim Genel Kurulu; sets and can revise the YKS-exclusivity policy and its three named exceptions; this layer cannot be varied by any individual university. Layer 2 (national exam/placement mechanism): ÖSYM's TYT/AYT/YDT structure, the OBP formula, the four score types, and the placement algorithm itself apply UNIFORMLY to every domestic-pathway programme nationwide — no university can set its own weighting, request supplementary evidence, or override an algorithmic assignment; this is the least university-discretionary layer found anywhere in this package. Layer 3 (university/programme, domestic pathway): the only genuine per-university/per-programme discretion here is (a) the proposed quota size and score-type for a given programme code, subject to YÖK approval, and (b) for the narrow named talent-exam programmes, the specific institution's own TYT threshold and audition/portfolio design. Layer 4 (foreign-national pathway — a separate system, not an override layer): each university independently sets its own accepted credentials (TR-YÖS/SAT/A-Level/IB/Abitur/diploma-only), minimum thresholds, and evaluation process — including, at some institutions, holistic elements such as a statement of purpose — for its foreign-national quota. This layer has close to full university discretion, the structural opposite of Layer 2/3's near-zero discretion, and — per the same reasoning as RULE-ADMISSIONS-014 — should be modeled as a parallel system rather than an override sitting on top of the domestic layers, since there is no shared domestic baseline being modified for this population.

matrix_row.main_application_architecture: Fully centralized, algorithmic score-based placement (not an application/decision platform in the Western sense) for the domestic pathway; fully decentralized, university-independent evaluation for the separate foreign-national pathway
matrix_row.central_platform: ÖSYM (Ölçme, Seçme ve Yerleştirme Merkezi) — administers YKS (TYT/AYT/YDT) and TR-YÖS, computes placement scores, and RUNS the actual centralized placement/matching algorithm for the domestic pathway (a genuine decision-making engine, not registration-only); for the foreign-national pathway ÖSYM administers TR-YÖS exam logistics only — admission decisions there are made independently by each university
matrix_row.direct_applications_possible: Not in the domestic pathway — no student ever applies to an individual university; placement is by centralized algorithm from a single national preference list. Yes, and the default, in the separate foreign-national pathway — each university runs its own independent application/evaluation process
matrix_row.application_choice_limits: Up to 24 programme-code preferences on ONE unified national list per candidate (spanning ön lisans and lisans codes together), not per-university; list need not be filled
matrix_row.predicted_grades_role: Does not exist as a concept — no application timeline requires a forward-looking projection; only final, actual diploma grade (OBP) and final, actual exam scores are ever used
matrix_row.subject_prerequisites: No named-subject checklist; subject specialization is enforced entirely through the SAY/EA/SÖZ/DİL score-type mechanism — which AYT subject cluster a candidate sits determines which programmes they can even be ranked for
matrix_row.standardized_tests: YKS (TYT+AYT+YDT) is not a supplementary factor — it is the central and near-exclusive admissions lever for the domestic pathway; TR-YÖS (or SAT/A-Level/IB/Abitur, university-specific) plays the equivalent role in the separate foreign-national pathway
matrix_row.language_proof: YDT (a YKS component) only relevant to Foreign Language/Translation-track programmes, not a general gate; separately, many programmes (especially English-medium ones) require YDS/YÖKDİL or a university-set equivalent for exemption from a mandatory English-medium preparatory year — but this is an enrollment/instruction gate applied AFTER placement, not an admission eligibility gate
matrix_row.essays_motivation: Does not exist in the domestic pathway — absent entirely; no programme in the standard pathway requests one. May appear as one additional criterion at specific institutions' foreign-national-pathway seats only (e.g. Boğaziçi)
matrix_row.recommendations: Does not exist in the domestic pathway — absent entirely, domestic or foreign-national, in every source reviewed
matrix_row.extracurricular_role: None — zero channel into the domestic placement score; confirmed independently by this research and by the counseling-intelligence research lane (RULE-COUNSEL-057/109)
matrix_row.conditional_offers: Does not exist as a meaningful concept — placement only ever happens after both the final diploma grade and final exam scores are already known; only a narrow procedural (document-submission) conditionality applies at registration
matrix_row.restricted_programmes: Universal, not exceptional — every lisans programme nationally has a hard YÖK-approved numeric quota and is filled by strict score-rank order; 'restriction' is a continuous, cycle-varying cutoff-score/rank rather than a binary open-vs-capped category. Named non-exam-score exceptions: state conservatory, fine arts, sports sciences, some education-faculty performance programmes (TYT threshold + talent/audition exam)
matrix_row.turkiye_meb_direct_entry_complexity: [Repurposed for Turkey's own row, per this package's schema-consistency convention: describes how FOREIGN-curriculum students enter Turkish universities.] Structurally simple relative to the complexity every OTHER country's row reports for a Turkish applicant, but bifurcated by registration location, not curriculum: a genuinely foreign-schooled applicant (secondary education completed entirely outside Turkey/TRNC) — via IB, A-Level, Abitur, or any national curriculum — enters through the fully decentralized foreign-national pathway (TR-YÖS or a university-accepted alternative: SAT, A-Level, IB Diploma, Abitur, diploma-score-only at many foundation universities), each university independently setting its own accepted credentials and minimum thresholds — no centralized placement algorithm governs this population. By contrast, a student who completed IB/A-Level/AP AT A SCHOOL IN TURKEY (Turkey/TRNC-registered) is generally NOT eligible for this route and must instead sit YKS like any other Turkey-registered candidate, regardless of curriculum — the foreign-curriculum content itself does not open an alternate admission channel domestically. Narrow named exceptions (embassy-school students; MOBİS-listed international private institution students; specific MEB-project-relocated foreign nationals) remain foreign-pathway-eligible even while resident/schooled in Turkey.
matrix_row.dominant_counselor_risk: Applying a holistic-review or threshold-eligibility mental model (the shape of every other country in this package) to a system that is neither — specifically: (1) treating OBP or the diploma grade as a holistic signal a counselor could help 'strengthen the narrative' around, when it is a fixed numeric multiplication; (2) recommending extracurricular/leadership/research investment as an admissions lever for a domestic-YKS-track student, when zero channel exists for that evidence to matter; (3) conflating the domestic YKS pathway with the separate foreign-national pathway — assuming TR-YÖS results are centrally placed the way YKS is, or assuming a Turkish citizen/resident is automatically YKS-track when their actual schooling was foreign or their stated target is a different country entirely. All three risks stem from the same root: this is the first country in the package where the correct model is 'centralized algorithmic placement with zero non-academic evidence,' not a variant of holistic review, threshold eligibility, or formula-plus-officer-judgment.
